target_customer: Enterprises moving large data over hard networks: satellite and ground stations, drone fleets, robotics, AI clusters, media and defense
problem: TCP based transfers are slow and fragile over long, lossy or non-IP links. Byteport sells a UDP based protocol it says is far faster and lossless.
business_model: Software subscription: Growth plan $500 per month ($425 annual) and custom enterprise pricing, plus custom network builds
product_category: High speed data transfer protocol and software (DART)

founders.name: Jayram Palamadai
founders.background_notes: A Fondo interview says he worked at CERN as a distributed computing engineer moving collider data. Education not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: A custom transport protocol over UDP needing congestion control, reliability and SDKs across many languages, plus non-IP and radio network work. Protocol engineering is hard, and the headline speed claims are not independently benchmarked.

defensibility.rationale: A proprietary protocol embedded in customers' pipelines would be sticky, but Aspera, Signiant and other UDP transfer products are established alternatives.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established file transfer vendors exist but no response to Byteport found; it has almost no press coverage.

market_need_then: Satellite, robotics and AI cluster operators move large volumes over poor links, and alternatives to Aspera are widely discussed. Direct demand evidence for Byteport, such as named customers, was not found.

branding.domain_note: Consolidated from byteport.io to byteport.com per a Huge Magazine profile (early 2026)

identity.voice_and_tone: Heavy on superlatives and reliability language such as mission-critical and battle-tested

branding.brand_signature: DART, short for Dynamic Accelerated Record Transfer per the YC page
branding.community_and_virality: Fondo startup podcast interview and one independent review that notes no press coverage and no verifiable traction

brand_strength.rationale: Name is clear for the byte and port idea, and the exact .com was secured. Speed claims vary across the site (10x, 100x, 1500x), which hurts credibility.

outcome_analysis: Early and active with no public outcome. The CEO's CERN experience moving collider data fits the problem, and the product is priced from $500 per month. Funding and customers are unconfirmed and the performance claims are inconsistent, so traction is the key unknown.
notes: VCBacked lists $500K pre-seed in Mar 2026 from Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund and CB Insights lists $500K from Spot VC; both are aggregators and disagree on stage and investors, so no round is recorded. The Fondo interview names no funding. Competitor sources seen were undated vendor comparison blogs (Aspera, Signiant, Raysync, Filemail), so the dated list is empty. YC page team size is 4. No outcome news found.
